site.title: Godot Scene Series
site.tagline: Short animations that show how to build each piece of a 2D game, one scene tree at a time.

topics.title: Players
topics.blurb: Five ways to set up a player scene, and how to pick the right body for your game.

topics.title: Pickups
topics.blurb: Coins, hearts and keys: items that notice the player and handle themselves.

topics.title: Enemies
topics.blurb: Things that move on their own, patrol, chase, and hurt the player.

topics.title: Tilemaps
topics.blurb: Painting levels from tiles, with collision built right into the tiles.

topics.title: UI
topics.blurb: Scores, health bars and menus that sit on top of the game.

bigIdeas.title: Pick the body by what it needs
bigIdeas.text: Area2D notices overlaps but never blocks. CharacterBody2D moves the way your code says and stops at walls. RigidBody2D lets the physics engine move it. When in doubt, a player starts as a CharacterBody2D.

bigIdeas.title: Every body needs a shape
bigIdeas.text: Area2D, CharacterBody2D and RigidBody2D have no size of their own. A CollisionShape2D child gives them one. A detection only happens when two shapes overlap, so both sides need a shape. Godot shows a warning triangle until you add one.

bigIdeas.title: Items handle themselves
bigIdeas.text: A coin is its own scene with its own Area2D. It notices the player with body_entered and removes itself with queue_free(). Give the player its own Area2D only for the exceptions: a magnet radius, an interaction range, or a hurtbox.

bigIdeas.title: Top-down: the shape goes at the feet
bigIdeas.text: In a top-down game, keep the player's collision shape small and at the feet. The head and body can then pass in front of walls and trees, which makes the 3/4 view look right.

bigIdeas.title: One Input Map, same names everywhere
bigIdeas.text: Make the actions move_left, move_right, move_up, move_down and jump once in Project Settings, Input Map. Input.get_vector() turns the four moves into one direction, and moving diagonally isn't faster. Input.get_axis() does the same for one axis.

bigIdeas.title: Move bodies in _physics_process()
bigIdeas.text: Code that moves a CharacterBody2D or pushes a RigidBody2D goes in _physics_process(delta), so it runs in step with the physics engine.

episodes.title: Platformer player
episodes.summary: A side-view player that runs, jumps and lands on the ground.

episodes.title: Top-down player
episodes.summary: A player that walks four ways, stops at walls, and lets coins handle themselves.
episodes.code:
var dir = Input.get_vector(
    "move_left", "move_right",
    "move_up", "move_down")
velocity = dir * SPEED
move_and_slide()

episodes.title: Arcade dodger player
episodes.summary: An Area2D player that moves by position, stays on screen, and notices when it gets hit.
episodes.code:
position += dir * SPEED * delta
position = position.clamp(
    Vector2.ZERO, screen_size)

episodes.title: Physics player
episodes.summary: A rolling ball you push with forces; gravity, bounces and momentum come from the engine.

episodes.title: Which body should my player be?
episodes.summary: Area2D, CharacterBody2D and RigidBody2D walk at the same wall. One walks through, one stops, one bounces.

episodes.title: A coin that collects itself
episodes.summary: Coin.tscn: an Area2D that notices the player with body_entered, adds to the score, and removes itself.

episodes.title: Hearts and signals
episodes.summary: A heart pickup that heals, and a signal that tells the rest of the game it happened.

episodes.title: Magnet pickups
episodes.summary: The exception: a player-owned Area2D with a big radius that pulls coins in from far away.

episodes.title: A patrolling slime
episodes.summary: A CharacterBody2D enemy that walks back and forth and turns around at ledges with a RayCast2D.

episodes.title: Hitboxes and hurtboxes
episodes.summary: Two Area2Ds that find each other, kept apart from walls with collision layers and masks.

episodes.title: Chase when close
episodes.summary: A detection Area2D that starts a chase when the player walks in and stops it when they leave.

episodes.title: TileMapLayer basics
episodes.summary: Make a TileSet from a tile sheet and paint a level with a TileMapLayer.

episodes.title: Collision in the tiles
episodes.summary: Add a physics layer to the TileSet and draw collision onto tiles, so painted walls block the player.

episodes.title: Y-sort for top-down
episodes.summary: Let the player walk behind trees and in front of them, sorted by how far down the screen they are.

episodes.title: A score on screen
episodes.summary: A CanvasLayer HUD with a Label that stays put while the camera moves.

episodes.title: A health bar
episodes.summary: A TextureProgressBar that updates when the player's health changes, wired up with a signal.

episodes.title: Pause and game over
episodes.summary: Menus that pause the game tree and buttons that restart or quit.
